comment: A dollar isn't going to make me leave, honestly. My real gripe is that Discover Weekly and song radio keep handing me stuff already sitting in my library. Fix the recs and I'll happily pay the extra buck.

Honestly the full catalog for eleven bucks is still a steal, and if it means artists get paid a bit more per stream I'm all for it. Tidal can talk about artist payouts all it wants, but I'm staying put for now.

Price goes up a buck and the per-stream royalty still rounds to fractions of a cent for the artist. Spotify is raising prices while artists are still getting crumbs, so the money is not going where people think it is.

Apple Music is already lossless with Spatial Audio for basically the same money, and now Spotify wants more for the same thing without better sound. I think this is the nudge I needed to go back to Apple Music, the desktop app and Connect aren't worth much more.

Cool, more money for shuffle that still isn't random!!! I can't even get a true shuffle through my own playlists without the algorithm stepping in. Price hike means nothing when the basics are broken.

Great, they're charging more for a product that still won't let me see liked songs inside a playlist or add duplicates on mobile. I already left once over playlist stuff, so if they keep dropping the things I actually use, I'm done paying.

A buck more is annoying but Premium still does a lot for the money, so I'm not bolting over it. My bigger worry is the free tier getting more ads, because that's what makes the paid plan worth it in the first place.
Family plan going to $16.99 is still a few bucks per person for us, which beats paying for ads. We're keeping it, though I wish the duo and family setup weren't so confusing to switch into.

I already cancelled my family plan over the podcast-stuffed home screen, so this price bump just confirms I'm not paying for a service that keeps shoving shows at me. Show me the music, not another price increase.
Student plan going from $4.99 to $5.99 hurts, and I literally said I'd go back to Apple Music if this happened. Hulu is still included, but I'm on a tight budget so I'm switching back.

Price going up when the UI keeps getting worse every redesign is a tough sell. Recommendations are still stale and the home page is a mess, so I'm watching this closely and YouTube Music is looking better every update.
Another price increase and still no lossless. Tidal and Deezer already give hi-fi at similar prices, so Spotify is asking for more while the sound stays the same. I'm moving to Tidal full time.
Price going up is fine on paper but I'd rather they fix the bugs first. Every update I'm reinstalling, rolling back, and waiting on support, and downloads still won't play offline.
I'm not even paying anymore, but the renew subscription pop-up is still hitting me every time I open the app. Reinstalled, cleared cache, nothing. Anyone know how to get rid of this thing?

Still worth it. Ad-free, offline downloads and casting for a price rise of a dollar is fine with me, and it's still way better value than the free tier. The app itself is my real complaint but I'm not canceling over this.
Paying more so I can still get ads in podcasts and get shoved more shows? No thanks. If they keep pushing podcasts and ads keep playing on Premium, I'm going to YouTube Premium.
Absolutely hate this update, and now they want more money for it. If the new music tab layout stays I'm switching to Apple Music, I'm done with the extra taps and the autoplay nonsense.

Price going up while the features I want are still gone. Probably rolling out slowly to some users, I'd bet this is about the UI sticking. Vote with your wallet, people, and vote in those feature requests too.

A price increase on the family plan while they keep the TikTok-style home screen? This is garbage. I'm considering canceling my subscription and moving to Apple Music or Tidal, I'm done paying for this junk.
Can't afford it some months as it is, so an extra dollar is just making it harder. I'll probably cancel the plan and go back to the free version, and I'm sick of the renew prompts after I cancel too.
Price going up doesn't change much for me since I'm running an older version anyway. If they force the new layout through a update I'll cancel again, same as last time.

A price increase doesn't do much for me since I'm still on free, though I was kind of tempted to resubscribe. Free is fine as long as the ads are tolerable, and skipping songs on Premium is still what I'd pay for.
Cool, they raise the price and still no liked songs on album track lists. If they keep taking features away I'll unsubscribe again, because right now this isn't worth money.

Paying more for a service where I can't see my liked songs in playlists, can't share playlists, and get autoplay video ads while I browse? I'm switching back to Apple Music, and I might just unsubscribe for good.

A dollar is nothing if they add features back, but right now the radio keeps repeating songs I already know and the play counts are still hidden. Stats.fm is the only way I get any real data, so I'm staying and hoping for better.
Spotify still has no lossless tier and now they want more money. Tidal pays artists better and sounds better, so I'll keep my HiFi there and only use Spotify for Connect.
